The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the top-level of the PKGBUILD and does not execute functions such as `package()`, `build()`, `prepare()`, or `pkgver()`. In this file, all variable assignments (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, etc.) are static and do not involve command substitution or dynamic code execution. The `source` array references a Git repository via the declared upstream URL with a tagged release (`v$pkgver`), which is standard practice for VCS packages. Notably, there is no use of command substitution (e.g., `$(...)` or backticks), `eval`, network requests, or file system modifications at the global scope. The `sha1sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal for VCS sources and does not pose a risk during `--printsrcinfo`, as no downloads or verifications occur in this phase. All content in the PKGBUILD up to the `package()` function is declarative and safe to parse.

While the `package()` function contains logic to locate site-packages and install desktop/icons files, that function is not executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and thus poses no risk at this stage. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction presents no immediate security threat.
</details>
